title: Simulate FCFS, SJF, and SRTF and measure turnaround, waiting, and response time
brief: Turn a list of jobs into a Gantt timeline under three policies, then compute the three numbers that tell you which policy is better.
hints: Sort the jobs by (arrival, name) first. FCFS then walks that list, and the clock is max(clock, job.arrival) before each job so an idle CPU waits for the next arrival.

SJF is non-preemptive. When the CPU becomes free, build the list of jobs with arrival <= clock and pick min by (burst, arrival, name). If that list is empty, jump the clock to the earliest arrival still pending.

For SRTF, step the clock one tick at a time. At every tick pick min by (remaining, arrival, name) among arrived, unfinished jobs, run it for one tick, and append (name, t, t + 1). Then call merge_slices.
Idle time is not recorded. If no job has arrived at tick t, jump to the earliest arrival that is still unfinished instead of looping one tick at a time.
turnaround = completion - arrival, response = first start - arrival, waiting = turnaround - burst. Completion is the largest end among a job's segments; first start is the smallest start.
